answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before it can submit jobs or claim rewards; the kernel records the bond and links payouts to a persistent identity key. A quill of reputation is earned only after independent peers verify completed work, so copying profiles does not copy trust. If a challenged claim fails, the bond is slashed and the cedar of linked accounts can be audited for shared funding. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up real capital across identities and risks losing it, while newly created accounts still lack useful reputation.
